misconception_description: Student believes that modifying a for loop variable inside the loop body does not affects the next iteration's value.

solutions.generated_code:
program CariTerkecil
kamus
  n, i, x, terkecil : integer
algoritma
  input(n)
  for i <- 1 to n do
    input(x)
    if i == 1 then
      terkecil <- x
    else
      if x < terkecil then
        terkecil <- x
      endif
    endif
    i <- i + 1
  endfor
  output(terkecil)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student adds a line `x = min_val` when encountering a value larger than the current minimum, believing this will "skip" or "optimize" the iteration by resetting x to the minimum value. The student thinks this modification affects subsequent loop iterations, making the loop more efficient by avoiding unnecessary comparisons with large values. In reality, modifying the loop variable x has no effect on the iteration - the for loop will continue with the next element from list1 regardless. The code still functions correctly and finds the minimum value, so this is a benign misconception that results in unnecessary but harmless code.
